news_drafts.headline: Dumfries and Galloway projects £764k overspend on Supporting Learners and £253k on primary schools
news_drafts.lead:
Dumfries and Galloway Council's education service projects overspends on two budget lines for 2026/27: £764k on Supporting Learners and £253k on primary schools. The figures are in the second-quarter revenue budget monitoring report for the Education, Skills and Community Wellbeing Committee, which meets on 10 November.

Supporting Learners has a projected out-turn of £22.705m against a revised budget of £21.941m. Additional support for learning (ASL) generic support is the largest single variance. It is projected at £1.143m over its revised budget of £13.149m. Education Psychologists, Sensory Services and Targeted Support are each projected under budget.

The primary schools line, which includes Learning Centres, has a projected out-turn of £60.288m against a revised budget of £60.035m. The paper records a £1.038m budget adjustment in 2026/27 before that revised budget was set.
news_drafts.paper_title: ESCW Q2 Revenue Budget Monitoring 202627 Appendix 1

news_drafts.headline: Dumfries and Galloway: Dumfries Academy and Loreburn Primary allocation left a gap of about £10m
news_drafts.lead:
The money Dumfries and Galloway Council had agreed for Dumfries Academy and Loreburn Primary School does not cover the costs identified for the two schools, leaving a funding gap of around £10m. The figure is in an appendix to the council's capital investment programme, its planned spending on things that last, such as buildings, over the next few years.

The council's Education and Learning Committee agreed on 23 May 2024 that the existing allocation was not enough. That allocation is part of £73.975m in the programme. The appendix says: "Previously agreed capital allocation (part of the £73.975m) is not enough to cover the values identified, so Members also agreed to request the funding gap, circa £10m, from FTP committee."

FTP is the Finance, Procurement and Transformation Committee. The papers quoted here do not say how that committee responded to the request.

news_drafts.headline: Dumfries and Galloway council secures £50m Levelling Up grants but faces social care audit concerns
news_drafts.lead: The council has received over £50 million from the UK Government's Levelling Up Fund. Its capital projects — spending on buildings and other long-lived assets — are delivering on schedule: the Stranraer Watersports Hub is due to open in September, the Dalbeattie Rocks and Wheels facility is nearing completion, and the George building has attracted eight expressions of interest with a tender exercise in progress. The internal audit's overall opinion is Reasonable, meaning there is a generally sound system of governance, risk management and control in place. However, auditors have flagged two areas requiring ongoing monitoring: social care budgets and IT procurement, indicating these carry elevated risk requiring continuous attention.

findings.paper_title: IJB q2 Additional Funds from change fund breakdown 2.8m - Appendix 3
findings.headline: Posts marked with an asterisk are funded from Dumfries and Galloway Council corporate change funds, with £342k remaining and vacancies in the team.
findings.detail: The footnote says these posts are funded from DGC corporate change funds with a view to offsetting cost reductions beyond this period. It also notes that the team has current vacancies and that £342k remains in the change fund.
findings.matters: A finance officer elsewhere can compare how a council funds posts from corporate change reserves against expected cost reductions, and how much of that reserve is left.
findings.quote: These posts are currently funded by DGC corporate change funds with view to offsetting cost reductions

findings.paper_title: IJB q2 Additional Funds from change fund breakdown 2.8m - Appendix 3
findings.headline: The paper lists an Ongoing Allocation of £1,025,500 and £1,774,500 available to offset or allocate in FY27/28 from the £2,800,000 change fund.
findings.detail: The summary splits the allocation into an ongoing FY27/28 amount and a balance available for FY27/28. The table includes an Innovation Fund line, estimated at 125.0 in £k, marked 'New - Time Limited'.
findings.matters: It shows how much of the change fund is set against recurring FY27/28 costs and how much remains unallocated, which bears on how the posts are funded beyond FY26/27.
findings.figures: Ongoing Allocation £1,025,500; Available to offset/allocate in FY27/28 £1,774,500; Innovation Fund estimate £125.0k

findings.paper_title: IJB q2 Additional Funds from change fund breakdown 2.8m - Appendix 3
findings.headline: The paper shows £410,725 of the £2,800,000 change fund allocation as existing usage in FY26/27, with £2,389,275 listed as available to offset or allocate.
findings.detail: The Financial Recovery Plan lists a Change Fund Allocation of £2,800,000. It shows existing usage in FY26/27 of 410,725 and existing committed FY26/27 of 230,500, and gives an estimated FY26/27 requirement of 411 in £k.
findings.matters: A finance director here or at another council can see how much of a £2.8m change fund is drawn, committed and still unallocated against a recovery plan in the same year.
findings.figures: Change Fund Allocation £2,800,000; Usage in FY26/27 £410,725; Committed FY26/27 £230,500; Available to offset/allocate in FY26/27 £2,389,275; Estimated requirement FY26/27 £411k

findings.headline: Care at home hours delivered fell from 9,500 to 8,800 per week over the first 21 weeks of 2026/27.
findings.detail: The paper links the reduction to care package controls and recycling, and says it will continue to assess the wider effects on hospital flow, waiting lists, provider sustainability and service user outcomes.
findings.matters: A fall in delivered care hours is the mechanism behind the savings, and the paper names the side effects other councils would need to monitor if they pursue the same route.
findings.figures: 9,500 hours per week at start; 8,800 hours per week after 21 weeks; 700 hours per week reduction
findings.quote: reduction in care at home hours delivered from 9,500 hours per week to 8,800 hours per week

findings.headline: The paper states the forecast overspend is a financial risk to the Council because the IJB would seek an additional payment from the delegating body.
findings.detail: Under the agreed Integration Scheme, an overspend by the IJB would be recovered from the council as the delegating body. The paper says the IJB must continue to deliver savings to address the projected overspend.
findings.matters: A finance director or lender needs to know that an Integration Joint Board overspend can be passed back to the council under the Integration Scheme.
findings.figures: £5.1m Quarter 2 forecast overspend; £4.2m after planned savings
